environment: Spring king tides bring out citizen scientists along the Queensland coast
Great Barrier Reef scientists gear up for this year's coral spawning watch
science: Queensland researchers track humpback whale numbers as the migration season peaks
sports: Finals fever hits as the NRL and AFL finals roll into their biggest weekend
stories.overview: Thousands of humpback whales cruise past the Queensland coast in one of nature's biggest road trips

segments.title: The Open
segments.script: G'day and welcome to ParkSyde Bright Side, I'm Alex Mercer, and mate, it is a ripper of a Saturday out there. Spring's properly kicked in and Queensland is doing what Queensland does best, showing off. I'm Jamie, and honestly Alex, I've had my coffee outside on the balcony three days running now. That's basically the unofficial start of summer if you ask me. Bit premature Jamie, but I like the energy. Plenty on the show today, whales, reefs, finals footy and a weather chat with Sam, so let's get into it.

segments.title: Green Desk
segments.script: Let's start with the coast, because spring king tides are rolling through south east Queensland right now and local groups are out there doing tide watches and beach clean ups. It's one of those lovely low key community efforts that never really gets a headline but keeps our beaches in good nick. Yeah I love that one, no fuss, just neighbours grabbing a bucket and a bit of gumption. Meanwhile up north the reef crew are prepping their gear for coral spawning season, which usually fires up a bit later in the year after the full moon. It's basically the reef's version of a fireworks show, all those coral polyps releasing at once under the water. Scientists reckon healthy spawning events are a really good sign the reef is bouncing back in patches, which is the kind of good news we like around here.

segments.title: Science & Tomorrow
segments.script: Now sticking with the ocean theme, it is peak season for the humpback whale migration back down south, and Queensland's coastline is basically a whale highway right now. Researchers out of Queensland are out on the water counting numbers and checking in on mums with new calves. I saw a pod off Moreton Island last week and honestly Alex, nothing puts your Monday into perspective like a forty tonne animal doing a full breach for no reason other than it can. Scientists reckon these annual counts help them keep tabs on how the population's tracking after decades of recovery. Good news story right there, a species that was in real strife last century now cruising past our beaches in the thousands. Grab the binoculars this weekend, headlands from the Gold Coast right up to the Sunshine Coast are all in play.

segments.title: Weather
segments.script: Cheers Alex, and look, spring is well and truly in the driver's seat across the south east this weekend. We're looking at clear skies and light winds today, with Brisbane topping out around the mid to high twenties, so a properly pleasant one for the whale watching Jamie was just talking about. Sunday looks similar, maybe a touch of cloud building later in the day, but nothing to worry about for anyone heading to the coast or the footy. UV is climbing back into the danger zone though, so grab a hat, slip on the sunscreen and don't get caught out, it is sneaky this time of year. Back to you two.

segments.title: The Scoreboard
segments.script: Righto, footy finals are in full swing this weekend across both codes, and there is nothing quite like September footy to get the whole state talking. The NRL and AFL are both deep into their finals series, with prelims and cut throat qualifiers setting up the road to the big dance. The vibe around the pubs and clubs this week has been electric, everyone's got an opinion and half of Queensland reckons their team is a smokey. It's that classic finals tension, one bad half and your season's done. Exactly, win and you're still dreaming, lose and you're cleaning out the locker. Whoever you're behind, get among it this weekend, it's shaping up to be a cracker.

segments.title: Overview & Outro
segments.script: So there you have it, whales cruising the coast, reefs gearing up for their big spawning moment, and footy finals turning the whole state into armchair experts. Not a bad Saturday wrap if you ask me. Honestly my favourite kind of show, no drama, just good stuff happening in our own backyard. That whale migration story is going to have me staring at the horizon all weekend now. Ha, you and half of Queensland Jamie. Big thanks to Sam for the weather rundown, sounds like a beauty of a weekend to get outside. Absolutely, whether that's the beach, the footy, or just the backyard with a snag on the barbie. That's it from us today. I'm Alex Mercer, that's Jamie, this has been ParkSyde Bright Side. Get outside, look after each other, and we'll catch you next time.
